entries.prompt: To repair an old building and make it like new.
entries.why: Re- (again) + nov (new) + -ate (to make): to make new again.

entries.prompt: To build again something that was torn down.
entries.hint: The root struct means to build.
entries.why: Re- (again) + con- (together) + struct (to build): to build together again.

entries.prompt: To make a wall or a place stronger against attack.
entries.why: Fort (strong) + -ify (to make): to make strong.

entries.prompt: To clean, mend and freshen something so it looks new.
entries.hint: The root furb means to polish.
entries.why: Re- (again) + furb (to polish) + -ish: to polish and freshen a thing again.

entries.prompt: To put right something that is wrong.
entries.hint: The root rect means straight or right.
entries.why: Rect (right, straight) + -ify (to make): to make right.

entries.prompt: To join several parts into one strong whole.
entries.hint: The root solid means firm and whole.
entries.why: Con- (together) + solid (firm) + -ate (to make): to make firm by joining together.

entries.prompt: To make something steady so it will not wobble or fall.
entries.hint: The root stabil means firm, standing.
entries.why: Stabil (firm, standing) + -ize (to make): to make steady.

entries.prompt: To bring something back to good condition, so it can be used again.
entries.why: Re- (again) + habilit (able) + -ate (to make): to make able again.

entries.prompt: Sticking together well, so the parts hold as one.
entries.hint: The root hes means to stick.
entries.why: Co- (together) + hes (to stick) + -ive: sticking together.

entries.prompt: To save what can still be used from a wreck.
entries.why: Salv (safe) + -age: to save from loss.

entries.prompt: To form or build something up again from its parts.
entries.hint: The root stitut means to set up.
entries.why: Re- (again) + con- (together) + stitut (to set up): to set up again from its parts.

entries.prompt: A stitch that closes a wound.
entries.why: Sut (sewn) + -ure (the thing): a stitch that closes a wound.

entries.prompt: To make a wall or a frame stronger by adding support.
entries.why: Re- (again) + in- + forc (strength): to put strength in again.

entries.prompt: To get back health or strength after an illness.
entries.hint: The root cuper means to take.
entries.why: Re- (back) + cuper (to take) + -ate: to take back your strength.

entries.prompt: Able to be mended or put right.
entries.hint: The root par means to make ready.
entries.why: Re- (again) + par (to make ready) + -able (able to be): able to be made ready again.

entries.prompt: To make a bad thing better.
entries.why: A- (to) + melior (better) + -ate (to make): to make better.

entries.prompt: To shine light upon something; to light it up.
entries.why: Il- (upon) + lumin (light) + -ate (to make): to throw light upon.

entries.prompt: Giving off light; glowing in the dark.
entries.why: Lumin (light) + -ous (full of): full of light.

entries.prompt: A warm, bright glow given out by something.
entries.hint: The root radi means a ray.
entries.why: Radi (a ray) + -ance (the state of): the glow of something sending out rays.

entries.prompt: The moment when something catches fire.
entries.why: Ign (fire) + -ition (the act of): the act of catching fire.

entries.prompt: The tiniest bit of light there can be.
entries.why: Phot (light) + -on (a particle): one tiny bit of light.

entries.prompt: Glowing white with heat.
entries.hint: The root cand means to shine white.
entries.why: In- + candesc (to begin to glow white) + -ent: glowing white with heat.

entries.prompt: The burning of something, giving off heat and light.
entries.hint: It comes from the Latin comburere, to burn up.
entries.why: From the Latin comburere, to burn up: the act of burning.

entries.prompt: Giving off light without heat, as a glowworm does.
entries.why: Lumin (light) + -escent (becoming): beginning to glow, without heat.

entries.prompt: Shining brilliantly; dazzling to look at.
entries.hint: The root splend means to shine.
entries.why: Re- (again, intensely) + splend (to shine) + -ent: shining out brilliantly.

entries.prompt: Letting light pass through, but not clearly.
entries.why: Trans- (through) + luc (light) + -ent: letting light through.

entries.prompt: Glowing brightly when struck by light or other rays.
entries.why: Fluor + -escent (becoming): beginning to glow when rays strike it.

entries.prompt: To give off sparks or flashes; to twinkle.
entries.hint: The root scintill means a spark.
entries.why: Scintill (a spark) + -ate (to make): to give off sparks.

entries.prompt: A body that gives light, such as the sun or the moon.
entries.why: Lumin (light) + -ary (a thing that): a thing that gives light.

entries.prompt: Glowing faintly in the dark after the light has gone.
entries.hint: The first part, phos, means light.
entries.why: Phos (light) + phor (to carry) + -escent: carrying light, glowing on in the dark.

entries.prompt: A huge fire that spreads and burns far and wide.
entries.hint: The root flagr means to blaze.
entries.why: Con- (fully) + flagr (to blaze) + -ation: a fire blazing on every side.

entries.prompt: To flash and sparkle, as light on moving water.
entries.why: Corusc (to flash) + -ate (to do): to flash and sparkle.

entries.prompt: To bring water to dry land through channels and ditches.
entries.hint: A Latin root for watering sits in the middle.
entries.why: Ir- (into), rig (to water, from Latin rigare), -ate (to make): to bring water into the land.

entries.prompt: Giving something the water that it needs.
entries.why: Hydr (water) + -ation (the act of): the act of giving water.

entries.prompt: A long stone bridge or channel that carries water to a town.
entries.why: Aque (water) + duct (to lead): a channel that leads water.

entries.prompt: A pipe or channel that carries water.
entries.hint: Con- means together; the root means to lead.
entries.why: Con- (together) + duit (to lead): a pipe that leads water along.

entries.prompt: To flood a place with more water than it can hold.
entries.hint: The root und means a wave.
entries.why: In- (upon) + und (a wave) + -ate (to make): to flood over in waves.

entries.prompt: The state of being soaked so full that no more water can go in.
entries.why: Satur (full) + -ation (the state of): the state of being full of water.

entries.prompt: A lake made to store water for a town or farm.
entries.hint: The root reserv means to keep back.
entries.why: Reserv (to keep back) + -oir (a place for): a place where water is kept.

entries.prompt: To seep slowly down through soil or sand.
entries.hint: The root col means to strain.
entries.why: Per- (through) + col (to strain) + -ate: to strain through slowly.

entries.prompt: To drink in or soak up water, as a seed does.
entries.hint: The root bib means to drink.
entries.why: Im- (in) + bib (to drink): to drink in.

entries.prompt: To spread all the way through, as water through cloth.
entries.why: Per- (through) + me (to pass) + -ate: to pass all the way through.

entries.prompt: A layer of rock or sand underground that holds water.
entries.why: Aqui (water) + fer (to carry): a layer that carries water.

entries.prompt: Dipping something fully under water.
entries.hint: The root mers means to dip.
entries.why: Im- (in) + mers (to dip) + -ion (the act of): the act of dipping in.

entries.prompt: A flowing in, as water floods into a dry ditch.
entries.why: In- (in) + flux (flow): a flowing in.

entries.prompt: Rain, sleet, hail or snow that falls from the sky.
entries.hint: Pre- means before; cipit comes from the Latin for head, as in headlong.
entries.why: Pre- + cipit (head) + -ation: water falling headlong from the sky.

entries.prompt: To fill up a store of water again.
entries.why: Re- (again) + plen (full) + -ish, a verb ending: to fill up again.

entries.prompt: To give back water to something that has dried out.
entries.why: Re- (again) + hydr (water) + -ate (to make): to give water again.

entries.prompt: To let go of something, or set it free.
entries.hint: Re- means back; the root comes from a Latin word meaning to loosen.
entries.why: Re- (back) + lease (to loosen): to let go.

entries.prompt: To open up and show what was hidden.
entries.why: Dis- (undo) + clos (to close) + e: to undo what was closed.

entries.prompt: To set free from a cage, a chain or a cell.
entries.why: Liber (free) + -ate (to make): to make free.

entries.prompt: To take the chains off; to set free.
entries.hint: A fetter is a chain for the feet.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + fetter (a chain for the feet): to take off the chains.

entries.prompt: To free something that is caught or stuck fast.
entries.hint: Ex- means out; tric comes from a word for tangles.
entries.why: Ex- (out) + tric (tangles) + -ate: to get out of a tangle.

entries.prompt: An opening or a gap, such as a hole that lets in light.
entries.hint: The root aper means to open.
entries.why: Aper (to open) + -ture (the thing): an opening.

entries.prompt: To make wider or more open, as the pupil of an eye does in the dark.
entries.why: Di- (apart) + lat (wide): to spread wide apart.

entries.prompt: To unhook one part of a machine from another.
entries.why: Dis- (apart) + engage (to hook together): to unhook.

entries.prompt: A way out of a place.
entries.why: E- (out) + gress (to step): a way to step out.

entries.prompt: A way into a place.
entries.why: In- (in) + gress (to step): a way to step in.

entries.prompt: Easy to get into or reach.
entries.why: Ac- (to) + cess (to go) + -ible (able to be): able to be gone into.

entries.prompt: A grand doorway or gate.
entries.hint: The root port means door or gate.
entries.why: Port (door, gate) + -al: a grand door.

entries.prompt: To spread out a rolled-up flag or sail.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + furl (to roll up): to undo what was rolled up.

entries.prompt: To open a new building or event with a formal ceremony.
entries.hint: An augur read signs at the start of things.
entries.why: In- + augur (to read the signs) + -ate: to begin a thing with ceremony.

entries.prompt: To free from a heavy load that holds you back.
entries.why: Un- (undo) + en- (in) + cumber (to weigh down): to take off a heavy load.

entries.prompt: A mouth or opening, such as the end of a pipe.
entries.why: Or (mouth) + fice (to make): a made mouth, an opening.

entries.prompt: To begin to grow, as a seed puts out a shoot.
entries.hint: The root germin means a sprout or a seed.
entries.why: Germin (a sprout) + -ate (to make): to put out a sprout.

entries.prompt: To grow and spread quickly in great numbers.
entries.why: Proli (offspring) + fer (to bear) + -ate (to make): to bear more and more, and spread.

entries.prompt: To make something fresh and young again.
entries.why: Re- (again) + juven (young) + -ate (to make): to make young again.

entries.prompt: A substance in food or soil that helps living things grow.
entries.hint: The root nutri means to feed.
entries.why: Nutri (to feed) + -ent (a thing that): a thing that feeds.

entries.prompt: To make something greater or larger.
entries.hint: The root aug means to increase.
entries.why: Aug (to increase) + -ment: to make greater.

entries.prompt: Plants that grow in a place, taken all together.
entries.hint: The root veget means to be lively.
entries.why: Veget (to be lively, to grow) + -ation: the growing plants of a place.

entries.prompt: To carry the dust from one flower to another so it can make seeds.
entries.hint: The root names the yellow dust bees carry.
entries.why: Pollin (pollen, flower dust) + -ate (to make): to give a flower pollen.

entries.prompt: How green plants use sunlight to make their food.
entries.why: Photo (light) + synthesis (putting together): building food with light.

entries.prompt: The art of growing fruit, flowers and vegetables in a garden.
entries.why: Horti (garden) + cult (to tend) + -ure: the tending of gardens.

entries.prompt: The process of growing until fully developed.
entries.why: Matur (ripe) + -ation (the process of): the process of ripening.

entries.prompt: Growing thickly and richly, as a wild green meadow.
entries.why: Luxuri (growing rankly) + -ant: growing thick and rich.

entries.prompt: One small step by which an amount grows.
entries.hint: The root cre means to grow.
entries.why: In- (on) + cre (to grow) + -ment: a growth, one step larger.

entries.prompt: To grow longer; to stretch out.
entries.why: E- (out) + long + -ate (to make): to make longer.

entries.prompt: A bursting into flower; full bloom.
entries.why: Ef- (out) + floresc (to begin to flower) + -ence: a flowering out.

entries.prompt: To bring back to life, as rain does for a wilted plant.
entries.why: Re- (again) + viv (life): to give life again.

entries.prompt: To grow new plants from cuttings or seeds.
entries.why: Pro- (forward) + pag (to fasten) + -ate: to fasten forward, to breed more plants.
